summary: Short, temporary stays for people who support themselves. For example retired people and visiting academics.
who: People retiring to Ireland with their own income
Visiting academics at an Irish university or college
Elderly dependent relatives of an Irish citizen or of a non-EU resident
points: You cannot work or run a business, unless your letter of permission says you can.
You must support yourself fully, or your sponsor in Ireland must.
You cannot get state benefits or use publicly funded services, such as public hospitals.
You must have private medical insurance.
You must apply for Stamp 0 and be granted it before you can register.

work.title: No.
work.body: You cannot work or run a business, unless your letter of permission says you can.

description: Stamp 0 in Ireland: who gets it, why you cannot work, and the rules on money and medical insurance. Checked against official sources.

summary: Permission to work in Ireland, usually with an employment permit.
who: People working here on an employment permit
People with permission to run a business here
People on a Working Holiday Authorisation (you cannot renew this)
points: You can start a job only when you or your employer has an employment permit for it, or your letter of permission says you do not need one.
You cannot run a business or be self-employed, unless your letter of permission says you can.
After 2 years on a Critical Skills Employment Permit, or 5 years on another employment permit, you may be able to get Stamp 4.
Renew your permission before it ends if you want to stay.
Time on Stamp 1 counts towards citizenship.

work.title: Only the job on your permit.
work.body: You can work only in the job your employment permit is for, unless your letter of permission says otherwise.

description: Stamp 1 in Ireland: working on an employment permit, running a business, and the route to Stamp 4. Checked against official sources.

summary: Full-time, paid accountancy training with a company in Ireland.
who: Trainee accountants with a training contract at a company in Ireland
points: You can work only in your accountancy training job.
You cannot do any other business, trade or profession, unless your letter of permission says you can.
You must finish your accountancy training within 4 years.
To stay after it ends, renew before it expires or apply for another permission, such as an employment permit.

work.title: Only your training job.
work.body: You can work only as a trainee accountant under your training contract.

description: Stamp 1A in Ireland for trainee accountants: what work is allowed and the 4-year limit. Checked against official sources.

summary: Graduates of Irish colleges looking for work, and eligible spouses and partners of some permit holders.
who: Graduates with a level 8 award or higher from an Irish college (the Third Level Graduate Programme)
Spouses and de facto partners of Critical Skills Employment Permit holders, or of researchers on a Hosting Agreement
Since 15 May 2024: eligible spouses and partners of General Employment Permit and Intra-Company Transfer permit holders who have family reunification
points: You can work full time without an employment permit.
You cannot run a business or be self-employed.
Graduates get 12 months. With a level 9 award or higher, such as a master's, you can renew for 12 more months if you are actively looking for graduate work.
Graduates must apply within 6 months of getting their results. Use this time to find a job and get an employment permit.
Spouses and partners renew every year. After 5 years on Stamp 1G you may be able to apply for Stamp 4.
Time on Stamp 1G counts towards citizenship.

work.title: Yes, full time.
work.body: You do not need an employment permit while your Stamp 1G is valid. You cannot be self-employed.

description: Stamp 1G in Ireland: the graduate programme, spouses of permit holders, how long it lasts and working without a permit.

summary: Non-consultant hospital doctors (NCHDs) on a two-year multi-site General Employment Permit.
who: Doctors working as NCHDs on a two-year multi-site General Employment Permit
points: You can work as an NCHD in any public hospital or health care facility while your permit is valid.
Your employer must tell the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment before you change location or contract.
You and your family get conditions similar to Critical Skills Employment Permit holders.
Time on Stamp 1H counts towards citizenship.

work.title: Only as a hospital doctor.
work.body: You can work as an NCHD in public hospitals and health care facilities while your permit is valid.

description: Stamp 1H in Ireland for non-consultant hospital doctors on a multi-site permit: what it allows. Checked against official sources.

badge: 20 h a week in term, 40 h in holidays
summary: Full-time students on a course on the official list of approved courses (ILEP).
who: English language students
Undergraduate degree students
Master's and PhD students
Higher national diploma students
points: Your course must be on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes (ILEP).
You can do casual work without an employment permit: up to 20 hours a week in term, and up to 40 hours a week in the holidays.
The holidays are June, July, August and September, and 15 December to 15 January.
You cannot run a business.
You cannot get state benefits or use publicly funded services, such as public hospitals, unless you are entitled another way.
You can study in Ireland for 7 years at most.
English language students: at most 3 courses of 25 weeks, and at least 85% attendance.
Time on Stamp 2 does not count towards citizenship.
After you graduate, you may be able to move to Stamp 1G.

work.title: Yes, up to 20 hours a week.
work.titleHoliday: Yes, up to 40 hours a week.
work.body: Casual work only. You do not need an employment permit.

description: Stamp 2 in Ireland: 20 hours a week in term, 40 in the holidays, which dates count as holidays, and the 7-year limit.

summary: Full-time students on a course that is not on the official list (ILEP).
who: Students on a semester abroad at an Irish university or college
Students at a private secondary school
Spouses of some financially independent students
points: You cannot work or run a business.
You must have private medical insurance.
You cannot get state benefits or use publicly funded services, such as public hospitals.
Time on Stamp 2A does not count towards citizenship.
description: Stamp 2A in Ireland: students on courses outside the ILEP list, why you cannot work, and insurance rules.

summary: Permission to stay for a set time, without the right to work. For example volunteers and ministers of religion.
who: Volunteers, for example with a charity
Ministers of religion
Some family members of people here on an employment permit
points: You cannot work or run a business.
Renew your permission before it ends if you want to stay.
Time on Stamp 3 counts towards citizenship.
Spouse or partner of a General Employment Permit or Intra-Company Transfer permit holder? Since 15 May 2024, if you have family reunification you can get Stamp 1G and work without a permit.

work.title: No.
work.body: You cannot work on Stamp 3. If you are the spouse or partner of an employment permit holder, check if you can move to Stamp 1G.

description: Stamp 3 in Ireland: who gets it, why you cannot work, and the 2024 change that moved many spouses to Stamp 1G.

summary: Long-term permission to live and work. For example family of Irish citizens, refugees, and people who held an employment permit for some years.
who: People who held a Critical Skills Employment Permit for 2 years
People who held another employment permit for 5 years
Researchers who held a Hosting Agreement for 2 years
Spouses, civil partners and de facto partners of Irish citizens
Refugees, people with subsidiary protection, and family members who join them
Parents of an Irish citizen child
People granted Long Term Residence
points: You can work for any employer without an employment permit.
You can start and run a business.
You can work in a profession, if the professional body allows it.
You may be able to use state services. Each service decides.
Renew your permission before it ends.
Time on Stamp 4 counts towards citizenship.

work.title: Yes, any job.
work.body: You can work for any employer without a permit, and start your own business.

description: Stamp 4 in Ireland: who qualifies, working without a permit, starting a business and counting time for citizenship.

summary: Eligible non-EU family members of UK citizens who came to live in Ireland after 1 January 2021.
who: Non-EU family members of UK citizens living in Ireland
points: Your conditions are in your letter of permission. Read it carefully.
UK citizens themselves do not need permission. They can live and work in Ireland under the Common Travel Area.

work.title: Check your letter.
work.body: What you can do is set out in your letter of permission.

description: Stamp 4D in Ireland for non-EU family of UK citizens who moved here after 1 January 2021. Checked against official sources.

summary: Permission to stay without a time limit ("without condition as to time"). You can apply after 8 years of legal residence.
who: People with 8 years (96 months) of legal residence in Ireland
points: You can live and work in Ireland without an employment permit.
It does not give you a right to any particular public service. Each service decides.
You can apply after 8 years (96 months) of legal residence.
Stamp 5 lasts until your passport expires. Keep your passport valid.
Time on Stamp 5 counts towards citizenship.

work.title: Yes.
work.body: You can work in Ireland without an employment permit.

description: Stamp 5 in Ireland (without condition as to time): applying after 8 years, working, and keeping your passport valid.

summary: Irish citizens with a second citizenship. The stamp goes in their non-Irish passport.
who: Dual citizens who want their Irish status shown in their other passport
points: You are an Irish citizen, so you have no immigration conditions.
You do not need to register with immigration.

work.title: Yes.
work.body: You are an Irish citizen and have no immigration conditions.

description: Stamp 6 in Ireland: what it means for dual Irish citizens, and why you do not need to register.
